title: MouseWithoutBorders move relatively regression (with bisect)
summary: Mouse Without Borders relative movement on a three-monitor controlled PC can warp back to the same edge instead of handing off to the neighboring one-monitor PC.

judgment.rationale: The issue provides a concrete multi-monitor topology and regression bisect; the edge-handoff race remains a hypothesis to verify on current main.
evidence: The issue describes one monitor on PC 1, three side-by-side monitors on PC 2, relative movement enabled, and repeated warp-back when crossing the configured outer edge.
The reporter bisected the regression to c3c15ff; merged PR #27229 introduced UWP InjectMouseInput.
Current main neighbor detection remains in MachineStuff.MoveToMyNeighbourIfNeeded; the discussion does not prove the current branch still reproduces.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the relative-movement edge handoff on current main before implementing overlapping input-simulation changes.

fix_assessment.rationale: The historical bisect and exact repro support a likely handoff/injection issue, but current behavior must be confirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve relative-movement edge handoff
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Relative mouse injection may move the cursor beyond the neighbor threshold before the handoff decision observes the position; the existing discussion calls out queued input as a possible race.
plan: Reproduce the two-PC topology on a current build and trace received relative deltas through input injection and neighbor selection.
If the handoff reads a stale or wrapped cursor position, base the decision on a synchronized edge-crossing state rather than a single sampled point.
Add a regression test for batched positive/negative deltas crossing each outer edge.
verification: Verify repeated relative movement crosses from the controlled PC to its configured neighbor without warping back; also retain the high-polling-rate behavior introduced by #27229.

confidence.rationale: The reporter supplied a bisect and detailed race hypothesis, but it has not been revalidated on current main.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders relative movement on a three-monitor controlled PC can warp back to the same edge instead of handing off to the neighboring one-monitor PC.
known_information: The reporter gave a two-computer arrangement, relative-movement setting and explicit edge-crossing steps.
The reporter bisected the regression to commit c3c15ff, which introduced the InjectMouseInput path via merged PR #27229.
The follow-up discussion identifies asynchronous input injection and cursor-position sampling as a possible race, not a confirmed root cause.
inferences: The edge handoff may use a cursor coordinate that lags queued relative input; the reported bisect and discussion make this a testable hypothesis, not a proven current-main defect.
issue_context.analysis: The historic repro and bisect are unusually specific. Current main still performs neighbor selection in MachineStuff.MoveToMyNeighbourIfNeeded; reproduce before revisiting the injection-versus-handoff boundary.
initial_investigation: Read the full report and six comments; the reporter tried an edge clamp and found it insufficient when multiple deltas were queued.

reproduce.title: Verify Mouse Without Borders relative movement between two PCs
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable or current main; original regression reported in 0.72.0
prerequisites: Two Windows PCs on the same MWB setup; controller has one monitor and controlled PC has three side-by-side monitors.
setup: Arrange PC 1 to the right of PC 2 so the layout is `2 2 2 1`.
Enable “Move mouse relatively” on the controller.
steps: Use the mouse attached to PC 1 to move onto PC 2.
On PC 2, repeatedly move the cursor toward the right edge of its rightmost monitor.
Repeat from the opposite edge and compare relative movement on/off.
reproduce.expected_result: Crossing the configured outer edge should transfer the cursor to PC 1 instead of warping back to the left side of PC 2.
